title: VPC/On‑Prem Residency Evidence + SLA‑aware Failover Orchestration Playbook
creator: Priya Shah
description: Create a reproducible operations playbook, orchestration primitives, and evidence-export pipeline to ensure we can: (1) prove data residency and retention settings for Private/VPC/on‑prem customers; (2) perform SLA-aware region failovers while generating immutable evidence packages for audits; (3) surface residency state and retention enforcement in the Console and audit logs.
background: Enterprise and regulated customers require demonstrable proof that inference requests, persisted logs, and cached artifacts remained within approved geographic boundaries and retention windows. Existing residency enforcement covers routing and node tagging, but lacks an automated, tamper-evident evidence export and a coordinated failover orchestrator that respects per-customer residency guardrails and retention obligations.
problem_statement: When an evacuation or regional failover is triggered (operator or automated), we currently rely on ad-hoc scripts and manual verification to collect residency evidence. This produces delays, inconsistent reports, and risk during audits. We need an automated, SLA-aware failover orchestration that (a) enforces residency constraints, (b) stages and packs cryptographic evidence of data location + retention settings, and (c) provides predictable rollback and notification behavior.
goals: Automate evidence capture for residency and retention state at failover time
Expose per-customer residency state and retention configurations in Console and audit logs
Ensure failover orchestration respects residency guardrails and produces an immutable evidence bundle for compliance
Limit customer-visible downtime to SLA targets when performing residency-constrained failovers
Provide a reproducible reporter artifact for auditors (signed manifest + storage hash)
non_goals: Re-architecting low-level KV cache replication (out of scope)
Replacing customer-side archival workflows (we will integrate, not replace)
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can perform a simulated region failover for a test tenant with private VPC and produce a time-stamped evidence bundle within 30 minutes
Evidence bundle includes node location attestations, retention policy snapshot, routing decision logs, and a signed manifest with SHA256 hashes
Console shows residency lock status and the active fallback lane per-tenant during and after failover
Automated tests cover at least three failure modes: graceful evacuation, abrupt node loss, and network partition
Playbook documents manual operator steps, rollbacks, and the post-mortem evidence checklist
design_decisions: Evidence format: use a gzipped tarball with JSON manifests + per-file SHA256; include a detached RSA signature from the control plane signing key
Retention snapshot model: capture effective retention settings (customer config + system defaults) as of the failover timestamp rather than trying to reconcile historical deletions

Failover orchestration: implement an orchestrator service that sequences (a) quarantine gating, (b) staged traffic shift to pre-approved fallback nodes, (c) evidence snapshot, and (d) final switchover commit
Region compatibility: fallbacks only allowed to regions explicitly permitted by customer residency policy; otherwise, orchestrator aborts and escalates
Evidence immutability: upload evidence bundles to customer‑segregated (or customer‑managed) storage with object-lock + retention enabled where supported
tradeoffs: Signing evidence at control-plane increases auditability but requires stricter KMS access controls; temporary KMS exceptions complicate offline upgrades
Generating full node-level provenance (file-level hashes across many shards) is expensive — we snapshot metadata plus representative checksums to balance cost vs confidence
Conservative failover (abort if residency constraints ambiguous) reduces blast radius but increases recovery time for some incidents
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (spike, 1 week): Prototype evidence bundle format and signing flow; produce sample tarball from a test cluster
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build orchestrator primitives for quarantine gating, staged traffic shift API, and evidence collector microservice
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Integrate with Console: residency lock UI, active-fallback indicator, evidence download links and retention snapshot viewer
Phase 3 (1 week): End-to-end e2e test harness and three simulated failure runs; create operator playbook and runbook
Phase 4 (1 week): Security review, KMS gating, and staged rollout to canary tenants with non-critical workloads
testing_plan: Unit tests for evidence manifest generator (schema + hash correctness)
Integration tests for orchestrator sequencing under simulated network partitions
Chaos test: kill region controller process during failover to validate rollback and partial-evidence handling
Acceptance test: auditor script verifies signature, compares manifest hashes, and validates retention snapshot formatting
rollout_playbook: Deploy orchestrator to staging and run three simulated evacuations with test tenants
Canary: enable evidence exports for 5 internal customers, monitor time-to-evidence and operator alerts
Gradual rollout: toggle per-tenant residency enforcement flags in 10% increments, monitor error rates and Console indicators
Full rollout: default enforcement on for Private and Dedicated clusters after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics
monitoring_and_metrics: time_to_evidence_seconds: histogram for evidence bundle generation
failover_success_rate: percent of orchestrated failovers completed without manual intervention
evidence_validation_failures: count of bundles failing auditor verification
console_visibility_latency: time between failover event and Console residency state update
security_and_compliance: KMS: use envelope encryption for signing keys; rotate keys per-security policy
Audit: record all orchestrator decisions to immutable audit log with trace IDs
Data minimization: evidence bundle includes metadata and checksums, never includes raw customer data unless explicit customer-managed export is requested
open_risks: Customers with legacy VPC setups may not support object-lock or required storage features for immutable evidence
Edge/offline on-prem nodes may not be reachable during failover, producing partial evidence bundles
Operational complexity: orchestrator must coordinate with autoscaling and placement controllers to avoid capacity cascades
